title: Georgia's 8th Congressional District General Election, 2026
description: The 2026 general election for Georgia's 8th Congressional District pits incumbent Republican Rep. Austin Scott, first elected in 2010 and a senior member of the House Agriculture and Armed Services Committees, against Democratic nominee Dr. Kelly Esti, a Navy veteran and PhD in public policy. The district covers more than 30 counties across middle and south Georgia and is rated 'Solid R' by nonpartisan analysts, making Scott the heavy favorite. Esti ran on a platform emphasizing affordability, education access, infrastructure, and visible constituent service. The race presents a contrast between Scott's long tenure and rural conservative record and Esti's call for new leadership focused on evidence-based policy and community engagement.
polling_note: No public opinion polls were found for this race. Nonpartisan election analysts including Cook Political Report rate the district as 'Solid Republican'.

candidates.name: Austin Scott
candidates.summary: Austin Scott is the incumbent U.S. Representative for Georgia's 8th Congressional District, first elected in 2010 and currently in his eighth term. He serves on the House Agriculture Committee (Vice Chairman), House Armed Services Committee, House Rules Committee, and House Permanent Select Committee on Intelligence, focusing on farm policy, military readiness, and rural development.

candidates.name: Kelly Esti
candidates.summary: Dr. Kelly Esti is the Democratic nominee for Georgia's 8th Congressional District, having won the May 19, 2026 primary with approximately 53.5% of the vote. A Navy veteran who served as a nuclear operator aboard the USS Henry M. Jackson, he holds a PhD in Public Policy from Walden University and has worked as a small business CFO, legislative aide, and municipal board member, emphasizing affordability, education, infrastructure, and visible constituent representation.

forecast.rationale: No public opinion polling exists for this race, which tempers confidence. However, the available race data strongly supports a safe Republican outcome: Austin Scott is a long-serving eight-term incumbent first elected in 2010; the district covers more than 30 rural counties across middle and south Georgia; and nonpartisan analysts (e.g., Cook Political Report) rate it 'Solid Republican.' Democratic nominee Dr. Kelly Esti is a credible challenger — a Navy veteran, PhD in public policy, and primary winner — but lacks the structural advantages, district partisanship, and incumbency to make the race competitive under current conditions. Given zero polling data, the margin estimate is inferred from the district's partisan baseline and Scott's prior performance.
